title: LiveMedBench-Ask1: Evaluating Ask-Before-Answer Behavior in Medical LLMs

contributions.purpose: Provides a controlled way to measure whether a single clarifying question improves medical advice quality.
contributions.mechanism: The Ask1 evaluation protocol: models may ask one clarifying question answered by a deterministic slot oracle, compared under three conditions (masked baseline A, Ask1 protocol B, unmasked upper bound C).
contributions.evaluation: Applied to GPT-4.1 and Qwen3-14B on 657 cases with one masked critical patient information slot, using rubric-based scoring.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce the Ask1 evaluation protocol, a controlled framework for measuring single-turn ask-before-answer behavior in medical LLMs using a deterministic slot oracle.

contributions.purpose: Supplies a contamination-free test set with controlled information gaps for the Ask1 protocol.
contributions.mechanism: Constructs a 657-case subset of LiveMedBench with exactly one critical patient information slot masked, across eight clinically relevant slot types.
contributions.evaluation: 657 cases with rubric-based evaluation inherited from LiveMedBench.
contributions.source_quote: We construct a 657-case subset of LiveMedBench with single-slot masking across eight clinically relevant slot types.

contributions.purpose: Shows that targeted questioning capability does not translate into better answers under single-slot masking.
contributions.mechanism: Compares rubric scores across the A/B/C conditions and traces the null result to minimal information headroom rather than question generation failure.
contributions.evaluation: Both models ask targeted questions well above chance (50.1% and 37.8% slot hit rates) yet B-A confidence intervals span zero for both models; the C-A gap is only 0.6-0.9 percentage points.
contributions.source_quote: We provide empirical evidence that targeted questioning capability does not improve answer quality under single-slot masking, attributing this to minimal information headroom rather than question generation failure.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Building on LiveMedBench (Yan et al., 2026), a contamination-free benchmark with rubric-based evaluation, we construct a 657-case subset where exactly one critical patient information slot is masked.

Our work complements these efforts by providing a controlled single-turn evaluation protocol. Unlike multi-turn approaches, our Ask1 protocol isolates the effect of a single clarifying question through deterministic oracle responses, enabling precise measurement of whether targeted questioning improves answer quality.

notes: Negative-result paper: asking a clarifying question yields no rubric-score improvement (B-A CIs span zero for both models). The paper attributes the null result to a limitation of its own experimental design (C-A headroom of only 0.6-0.9pp under single-slot masking), i.e., the protocol cannot demonstrate benefit.
